podcast.title: John Hughes Movie Soundtrack Success
podcast.body: OMD followed Simple Minds in successfully soundtracking a John Hughes movie, *Pretty in Pink*, with their song "If You Leave." "Or orchestral maneuvers in the dark, better known as OMD, who followed in simple minds footsteps and soundtracked a John Hughes movie, Pretty in Pink."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia

podcast.title: Pioneering All-Electronic New Wave
podcast.body: OMD was identified as one of the most significant bands of the Technopop era and among the first of the new wave generation to fully embrace all-electronic sounds. Their approach was rooted in a punk rock aesthetic, despite limited traditional musical ability, focusing on creating new sounds with synthesizers. "The perfect example of late 70s technopop from orchestral maneuvers in the dark, they were one of the first of the new wave generation to turn to all electronic sounds."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Punk Sensibility in Synthesizer Use
podcast.body: Members Andy McCluskey and Paul Humphreys described their self-taught approach to music-making with synthesizers as having a "punk rock aesthetic." Instead of merely thrashing a guitar, they would play with two fingers on synths, creating sounds the "human brain had never heard before," which they found exciting compared to "rock and roll cliches" of traditional instrumentation. "But you were coming up with... You were coming up with sounds that the human brain had never heard before, which was the cool thing about these new machines. That was the exciting thing about using electronics was it gave us access to a pallet of sounds that were new and exciting, rather than just repeating what we saw in the mid to late 70s, is, you know, just rock and roll cliches."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
